paras: Each theme reads two or three toolkits together.
A theme is one idea about public life, tested with what the toolkits measured and what we saw on site. Each theme is read on Malé, Villimalé and Hulhumalé in turn, then the three are compared.

rows.title: Roads are made for movement, not staying
rows.note: The street edge against how many people pass and how many stay.

rows.title: Shade dictates movement, not distance
rows.note: Where people walk and stop against where the shade falls.

rows.title: Built form vs public life
rows.note: Density and ground-floor use against what people do outside.

rows.title: Density is not the problem, poor design is
rows.note: Each plot’s density against its housing quality score.

rows.title: Vehicles take more open space
rows.note: Conflicts with motorbikes and scooters against the people counted in the same areas.
